observations: Validity is the sharpest discriminator: the baseline's eval-1 diagram does not parse (raw angle brackets '<seconds>'/'<SENDGRID_API_KEY>' in notes) — exactly the gotcha references/syntax.md documents; the with-skill run explicitly avoided it and passed.

Arrow semantics discriminate: baseline drew RabbitMQ legs as sync request arrows (eval-1) and invented an 'MQ-->>API: ack publish' reply while calling it fire-and-forget (eval-2); with-skill used -) async arrows consistently.
Size discipline discriminates: baseline's eval-3 'overview' diagram has 56 message arrows; with-skill's largest is 18.
Ask-vs-invent discriminates: in eval-0 the baseline shipped a plausible invented checkout (disclosed as 'typical'), the with-skill run asked 5 targeted questions and shipped nothing fabricated.

The only with-skill failure (eval-3) is over-conservatism: the prompt established 'customer notified' on cancellation, but the agent deferred it to a question instead of drawing the fact and flagging only the mechanism. Improvement candidate for the contract wording.

Non-discriminating assertions this round: 'given details appear', 'real flow shown', '402 branch', 'participants consistent', 'safe-core syntax' — both configs pass these; keep them as regression floor.

Infra caveat: no validator was reachable inside the runs (no MCP in session; background subagents had Bash/Write denied; mermaid-cli lacks puppeteer Chrome on this machine). With-skill agents correctly reported 'not validated' per the honesty rule; validity was graded post-hoc via mcp.mermaid.ai. Next iteration should run agents in the foreground so the allowlist applies, and/or with the mermaid MCP connected.
